deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is page 2 of a bookkeeping register, continued from p. 29 and onto p. 31. It is very probably Gauss's count of letters in his correspondence, by correspondent.

(A) Main ledger. Each row gives: running correspondent number n, name, number of letters a_n, and cumulative total S_n = S_{n-1} + a_n. The page continues from S_132 = 931 (Reinhard Dresden) and runs from n = 133 (Reissig, S = 932) to n = 192 ('Klub', S = 1212). The heaviest entries here are:
- Schumacher, 42 letters (976 -> 1018)
- v. Zach, 49 (1122 -> 1171)
- v. Zimmermann, 36 (1171 -> 1207)
- Thiele, 24 (1066 -> 1090)
- Seyffer, 18 (1026 -> 1044)
There are also institutional correspondents: Royal Society, Institut National, a Liquidationscommission, Klub. A cross (†) marks deceased correspondents: Schröter, Stimmel(?), Tamsen, Thiele, v. Zimmermann, Wynecken.

(B) Lower-right table: growth by year. Columns are: number of correspondents N, 'bis Ende' year Y, cumulative letters L, and a fourth number r.
- 1809: 123, 748, 66.5
- 1810: 138, 850, 69.4
- 1811: 153, 950, 71.7
- 1812: 167, 1019, 71.5
- 1813: 175, 1108, 72.6
- 1814: 192, 1212, 74.5
- 1815: 208, 1371, 79.5
- 1816: 221, 1508, 82.6

My reconstruction of r (not stated on the page): r is the mean number of letters per year, r = L/(Y - 1798.5) with Y taken as the end of the year (Y + 1). Equivalently, the divisor is 11.25 for 1809, 12.25 for 1810, ..., 18.25 for 1816. So Gauss counted from about October 1798, the start of his correspondence after he returned to Braunschweig.
Checks:
- 748/11.25 = 66.49
- 850/12.25 = 69.39
- 950/13.25 = 71.70
- 1019/14.25 = 71.51
- 1108/15.25 = 72.66
- 1212/16.25 = 74.58
- 1371/17.25 = 79.48
- 1508/18.25 = 82.63
The 1814 row (192, 1212) coincides with the end of the main ledger. The ledger therefore represents the state at the end of 1814; the 1815 and 1816 rows were added later.

(C) Right margin, bleeding into the next page: the list 1, 2, ..., 13, 16, 17, 18, 19, 24, 32, 33, 36, 42, 48, 49, 113, 120, 161. These are the distinct values of a_n over the whole register (the 161 is Olbers, 120 Lindenau, 113 presumably Bessel). On p. 31 Gauss builds the frequency distribution: number of correspondents f_k with k letters, then k*f_k, then the running sum.
- The f_k sum to 192 correspondents.
- The products k*f_k sum to 1197.
- After the corrections on p. 31 (+3 and +15) the total becomes 1212, matching this page.
errors: All 60 cumulative additions on this page are correct, from 931 + 1 = 932 through 1211 + 1 = 1212.
Row 174 (Vadas) appears in the manuscript with the number written as '194', which is a slip for 174.

Lower table: two of the yearly means are truncated rather than rounded. For 1813, 1108/15.25 = 72.66 is written 72.6. For 1814, 1212/16.25 = 74.58 is written 74.5. The other six values are correctly rounded.
Several digits (1100, 1101, 1105, ..., 1121) are overwritten, and 1508 in the last row is also corrected. The final values are all arithmetically consistent.

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely personal bookkeeping of Gauss's correspondence with simple running sums and averages. It shows his well-known habit of statistical record-keeping but contains no mathematical result. It is mildly interesting biographically (sizes of correspondences in 1814, implied start date about 1798.75).
